newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World unit launches convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: New World unit launches convertible bonds.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd's wholly-owned subsidiary New World China Finance Ltd on Tuesday launched a US$300 million issue of mandatorily convertible bonds, global co-ordinator HSBC Investment Bank Asia Ltd said.

The bonds were intended to be mandatorily convertible into shares of New World China Ltd (NW China), a wholly-owned unit of New World China Finance, on the occurrence of an initial public offering (IPO) of its shares by December 31, 1999, HSBC said.
There was an over-allotment option of US$50 million for the bonds which would mature on December 31, 1999, the bank said.
The issue price was 100 percent, with coupon at four percent payable annually.

The IPO conversion discount and the redemption premium would be set to give a spread of 140-160 basis points over three-year U.S. Treasury Bonds. The conversion discount would be set at a minimum of six percent to the IPO price.
HSBC Investment Bank Asia Ltd was the sole global co-ordinator, bookrunner and lead manager of the convertible bond issue.
The terms of the issue were expected to be finalised around the end of this month, after an international roadshow starting on Thursday in Singapore.
NW China would hold and manage very substantial property development and investment interests of the New World Group in China, the bank said.
The New World Group would use the net proceeds of the bond issue to finance its property development and investment activities in China, and as the Group's general working capital.
